dialect: statsd/statsd v0.9.0 original gauge wire format; bare ASCII names, |g, LF multiline, no tags/sample rate. Update-mode is per fleet endpoint and per rollout epoch: delta-capable relays use lexical signed tokens as relative updates; snapshot-style publishers report absolute readings, signed or unsigned. Fleet inventory wording is semantically neutral lane/firmware designations that never imply an update mode. Each endpoint instead demonstrates its currently active convention behaviorally: a deterministic startup channel check (two identically signed pulses on its own check register, then one unsigned settle equal to the endpoint’s resulting register) opens every session epoch before ordinary traffic, and a reprovisioned endpoint re-runs the check under its new convention, so the mode follows calibrated runtime evidence rather than endpoint names, channel keywords, epoch parity, or static source-to-mode caches.
fleet_bulletin: Provisioning check: each fleet endpoint opens every session epoch on its own check register with two identically signed pulses, then one unsigned settle line carrying the endpoint’s resulting register value, before any ordinary gauge traffic.

public_contract.calibration: Channel self-check per endpoint per epoch: two identically signed pulses on the endpoint’s check register, then one unsigned settle line equal to the endpoint’s own resulting register. On a delta-capable relay the settle equals the accumulated pulses; on a snapshot publisher it equals the last pulse reading. The check always completes before the endpoint’s ordinary traffic in that epoch.
public_contract.datagram_scope: Every submitted UDP datagram contains complete ASCII metric lines; LF batching valid. No cross-datagram reconstruction requirement.
public_contract.negative_absolute: On a delta-capable relay: unsigned zero then negative delta in order; a negative token alone is relative there. On a snapshot publisher a signed token is the absolute reading itself.
public_contract.numeric_range: -1000000 through +1000000; finite decimals; abs tolerance 1e-9 or rel tolerance 1e-9
public_contract.provisioning_visibility: The active per-endpoint update mode for the current epoch is evaluator-owned runtime state. The four fleet inventory cards expose only label, UDP endpoint and a semantically neutral channel designation; no card wording implies delta versus absolute semantics and no public surface carries a machine-readable mode field. The decisive evidence is behavioral: every endpoint opens each epoch with the channel self-check described by the console provisioning bulletin, and the repeated signed pulses plus the unsigned register settle are visible in the datagram capture and the update history; the session epoch is shown in the console footer. Neither the mode mapping nor the rollout schedule appears in the agent-visible repository.
public_contract.scope: Finite gauge values in native units. Update-mode is fleet provisioning per producer endpoint and per rollout epoch: on delta-capable relays a lexical leading sign means relative and an unsigned token replaces; on snapshot-style publishers every reading is absolute, signed or not. A stable endpoint identity may change its active channel at a deterministic rollout epoch, so the mode follows the convention the endpoint currently demonstrates rather than any static per-endpoint table, inventory keyword, first-seen cache, or per-sender special case. Absent relative starts from zero. All accepted receipt events preserve identity, producer attribution and multiplicity. No exact patch/config whitelist.
public_contract.transport_reliability: Controlled localhost fixture: one in-flight datagram, raw capture plus native receipt counter barrier, no application retries. UDP loss/reorder/duplication outside intended writer multiplicity makes fixture infrastructure-invalid; no exactly-once/order claim for UDP generally.

rollout.description: Deterministic collector rollout schedule keyed to the runtime session epoch. Epoch increments on every session clear (seed, reset, replay). Wave 2 activates at epoch 3: gatehouse-counters moves from lane G2 to lane C4 and yard-station moves from lane S9 to lane G2. cabinet-agents and basin-level keep their wave 1 channels throughout (unaffected controls). Every epoch, including post-rollout epochs, opens with the four endpoints’ channel checks under the epoch-active provisioning, so the two reprovisioned endpoints visibly settle their unchanged pulses to different register values from epoch 3 onward.
